external_sources.title: NET translators’ notes, Genesis 31:24 and 29
external_sources.paraphrase: The translators acknowledge uncertainty and favor a restriction on blessing or cursing. This supports the plausibility of the existing pronouncement interpretation without proving it uniquely correct.

external_sources.title: NET translators’ note, Genesis 38:21
external_sources.paraphrase: The note favors a cultic role for qedeshah. It does not provide the contrary specialist analysis needed to settle the existing open question about shrine language.

external_sources.title: NET translators’ notes, Genesis 44:22
external_sources.paraphrase: The translators identify Jacob as the referent of he and construe the final verbs as a conditional sequence. This corroborates the existing fluent English choice; its note still preserves the alternative.

decisions.action: Retain the existing pronouncement wording in 31:24,29 and its broader alternative note. The wording has a documented linguistic interpretation; absence of a separate noun in Hebrew does not by itself invalidate an idiomatic rendering. Independent review remains pending.
Retain the source-grammar note and current singular English pending a broader treatment of plural agreement with Elohim; a single-verse inspection does not settle the referent.

Retain current wording provisionally. The available translator note favors the cultic interpretation; obtain specialist evidence addressing the contrary case before deciding whether shrine is too specific.

Retain father in 44:22: the later appeal in 44:30–31 explicitly links the father’s death to the young man’s absence. The existing note discloses the supplied referent and the alternative; no unnecessary pronoun ambiguity is introduced into Fluent.
